nodes.name: Chemical corrosion coating
nodes.procedure: In a typical preparation procedure (Figure 1A), the NF was soaked in CoCl2 solution and corroded to form the hydroxide layer (NiCo(OH)x-COR) on the surface. In the corrosion process, the NF could serve as both the substrate and the Ni source, whose Ni atoms were oxidized into Ni2+, leached from NF, and dispersed closer to the Ni skeleton. Meanwhile, oxygen in water was reduced into OH-, which reacted with Ni2+ and Co2+ to form NiCo(OH)x, and bound tightly to the NF. Besides, the Cl- could accelerate the formation of the metal-hydroxide layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo(OH)x-COR shows metal-hydroxide nanosheets with length ~200 nm and thickness 172 nm. NiCo(OH)x-RE transforms to flattened surface layer with negligible thickness change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon corrosion, the NF was coated with metal-hydroxide nanosheets, with a length of ∼200 nm and a thickness of 172 nm (Figures 1B, S1, and S2). After further reconstruction, NiCo(OH)x-RE underwent a significant morphology evolution, transforming from loose oxide nanosheets to a flattened surface layer...

nodes.characterization_summary: No observable peaks except Ni metal characteristic peaks (PDF#4-850), attributed to low crystallinity of corrosion layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) of the samples revealed no observable peak except the characteristic peaks of Ni metal (PDF#4-850), which could be attributed to the low crystallinity of the corrosion layer (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo(OH)x-COR shows amorphous structure with disordered atoms and (111) plane of Ni substrate. NiCo(OH)x-RE maintains amorphous phase after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further determine the crystal structure of the nanosheets, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) was applied... the part with the disordered arrangement of atoms corresponded to the amorphous structure of NiCo(OH)x⋅COR, while the interplanar spacings matched well with the (111) plane of Ni from the substrate. For the NiCo(OH)x-RE sample (Figure 1D), the amorphous phase was maintained after reconstruction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform dispersion of Ni, Co, O. Bulk atomic ratio Co/Ni decreases from 0.052 to 0.006 after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the elemental mapping of NiCo(OH)x-COR and NiCo(OH)x-RE proved that the Ni, Co, and O elements were uniformly dispersed throughout the oxide layers (Figures S6 and S7). The semiquantitative analyses of energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping indicated that the bulk atomic ratio of Co/Ni decreased from 0.052 to 0.006 after reconstruction...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/Co ratio changes from 2.2 to 4.1, Co content decreases from 0.30 to 0.21 wt%. After reconstruction in KOH, Ni concentration 0.072 mg L⁻¹, Co 0.020 mg L⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To detect the ratio of Ni/Co accurately, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) was also applied. The results exhibit that the Ni/Co ratio changes from 2.2 to 4.1 (Figure S10) and that the Co content decreases from 0.30 to 0.21 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s peak shifts from 531.5 to 531.2 eV with Ov content increasing from 67.6% (NiCo(OH)x-COR) to 81.3% (NiCo(OH)x-RE). Co 2p: Co³⁺ increases from 69.8% to 82.1%. Ni 2p: Ni³⁺ decreases from 21.5% to 15.9%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak of fine-scanned O 1s negatively shifted from 531.5 to 531.2 eV after 1,200 CV cycles (Figure 1E). The calculated content of Ov increased from 67.6% (NiCo(OH)x-COR) to 81.3% (NiCo(OH)x-RE)... The normalized Co³⁺ content in NiCo(OH)x-COR was 69.8%, and it increased to 82.1% in NiCo(OH)x-RE... The content of Ni³⁺ in NiCo(OH)x-COR was 21.5% and decreased to 15.9% in NiCo(OH)x-RE.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo(OH)x-RE shows higher defect degree (I₅₂₈/I₄₅₇ = 1.069 vs 1.028). γ-NiOOH peaks appear earlier at 0.37 V vs Ag/AgCl.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks at 528 and 457 cm⁻¹ were attributed to the Niᴵᴵ-O vibration of Ni(OH)₂... The values of I₅₂₈/I₄₅₇ for NiCo(OH)x-COR and NiCo(OH)x-RE at OCP were 1.028 and 1.069... These peaks first appeared for NiCo(OH)x-RE at 0.37 V vs. Ag/AgCl...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo(OH)x-RE shows increased presence of free O-H groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) was also applied to analyze the OH⁻ component (Figure S31), which demonstrated the increased presence of free O-H groups in NiCo(OH)x-RE.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo(OH)x-COR contact angle 120.6°, NiCo(OH)x-RE decreases to 0° indicating superhydrophilic surface. NiCo(OH)x-ED and NiCo(OH)x-HT are hydrophilic but with nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the catalyst layer became superhydrophilic, with the contact angle decreasing from 120.6° to 0° (Figures 4B and S32).

nodes.characterization_summary: After 60 h stability test, Co/Ni ratio of NiCo(OH)x-RE remains 0.42 (negligible change from 0.41). Other catalysts show significant changes indicating corrosion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After undergoing stability tests, the Co/Ni value of NiCo(OH)x-RE was 0.42, which exhibited a negligible change compared with the original value of 0.41...

nodes.characterization_summary: HR Cl 2p spectra after 60 h stability test show few Cl⁻ species on NiCo(OH)x-RE surface compared to enrichment in other samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR Cl 2p spectra further confirmed these findings (Figure 4D). Different from the enrichment of Cl⁻ species in other samples, few Cl⁻ species were found on the surface of NiCo(OH)x-RE...
